property_summary: For every nonzero Ether deposit amount sent to C.receive by any sender, the reference contract accepts the deposit (call returns/succeeds) and increments depositsCount; the mutant's stricter require makes receive revert for all deposits (so some inputs — e.g., any amount>0 — cause the mutant to fail this property).

For any nonzero Ether deposit from any sender, the correct contract's receive() accepts the deposit (call succeeds) and increments depositsCount (so address(c).balance increases and depositsCount increases), whereas the mutant's stricter require causes receive() to revert for such deposits (failing the acceptance/increment rule).

For every admissible sender and nonzero deposit amount, calling C.receive should succeed (not revert) and increase depositsCount by exactly 1; the mutant's strict '>' require makes receive revert for any deposit, violating this universal increment property for some fuzzed amounts/senders.

For any sender and any nonzero wei amount, calling C's receive payable fallback always succeeds (does not revert) and thus the call returns normally; the mutant's stricter require causes such receive calls to revert for some inputs, breaking that universal success property.

For every nonzero deposit amount sent to C by any sender, the correct contract's receive() accepts the payment (call succeeds) and increments depositsCount by 1; the mutant's stricter require causes receive() to revert for such deposits, breaking this rule for some fuzzed amounts/senders.

For any payable call to receive, the reference contract never decrements depositsCount (it only increments when the deposit arithmetic check passes), while the mutant that removes the require can cause depositsCount to increase even when the checked arithmetic would have detected overflow—so the reference enforces that depositsCount after a receive is always >= prior value and will revert on inputs that would overflow, whereas the mutant does not revert and thus violates this safety.

For any incoming Ether amount and sender, calling receive on C either preserves non-decreasing depositsCount (depositsCount_after >= depositsCount_before) or reverts if addition would overflow; the mutant removes the require and therefore can increase depositsCount when the correct contract would have reverted (violating the non-decreasing-with-revert behavior).

For any caller and any inbound ether amount, a call to receive() on the correct contract either reverts when the increment would overflow or leaves depositsCount non-decreasing; the mutant (which removes the require) can increment depositsCount when the correct contract would have reverted, violating this rule.

For any caller and any Ether amount, calling receive on the correct contract either reverts on an overflow attempt or leaves depositsCount non-decreasing (depositsCount_after >= depositsCount_before); the mutant removes the require so it can increment depositsCount when the correct contract would have reverted.

For any caller and any Ether value, calling receive() on the correct contract either reverts when the increment would overflow or otherwise leaves depositsCount non-decreasing (depositsCount_after >= depositsCount_before); the mutant removes the require and can increment depositsCount in cases where the correct contract would have reverted.

For any nonzero deposit amount sent to C.receive, the reference implementation always increments depositsCount by 1 (so depositsCount after the call >= before + 1); the mutant that decrements breaks this invariant for some inputs (deposits), producing a smaller depositsCount.

Every single call to receive() increases depositsCount by exactly 1 (so depositsCount_after == depositsCount_before + 1); the mutant that increments twice violates this by producing +2 for some inputs.

For any sender and positive ETH value, the reference contract always increments depositsCount by 1 when receive() is called with value>0 (so depositsCount after a deposit is previous+1); the mutant forbids any deposit after the first, breaking this for some inputs.
